sam: ran nsys on a production-like midbatch and saw a cascade of cudamalloc stalls during matmul algo handoff. timeline attached.

jia: can you paste the perfetto snapshot? looks like workspace reallocation every N steps

sam: pasted below — short perfetto excerpt, hot = cuBlasLtMatmul algo switch + workspace alloc

sam: ```
PERFETTO TIMELINE
0.000 cudamallocAsync  size=64MB  -> blocked 12ms
0.012 cublasLtMatmul  algo=23 ws=0 -> fallback to algo=5 ws=32MB
0.024 cudamalloc  size=32MB -> 8ms
0.032 kernel Launch  -> queueing delay 4ms
```

ben: that pattern smells like our slot-finder heuristic picking big algo then failing to reserve workspace. did you repro with small workspace cap?

sam: yes — with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 and CUBlASLT_WS_LIMIT=16MB the probe picks algo=5 consistently and stalls go away

ciara: could be related to kv-cache warmup interleaving. If prefix cache grows, effective seq len spikes and algo probe picks larger algo. Can we instrument seq-lens in the trace?

sam: added seq-len markers in the next run, sending nsys summary: kernel time dominated by workspace memcpy at N=128

ben: propose two steps: (1) tighten slot-finder cost model to penalize workspace churn, (2) add a fallback time-SLO threshold to reject high-ws algos during midbatch

jia: agree. also add a lightweight pre-probe that samples input shapes and forces cublasLt algo query only on stable shapes

ciara: I'll open a small RFC and include perf diff from nsys (before/after). assign to eng-runtime sprint 27

perf-bot: deploy note: rolled perf build: runtime/slot-finder/patch-214 deployed to staging at 2026-03-17T09:14Z :rocket:

sam: thanks — running a 1h soak now on staging with KV cache warmup enabled

ben: if soak looks good, let's gate change behind canary with 10% traffic and a 5% throughput SLA rollback

jia: added unit for cuBLASLt probe and a mock for cudaMalloc behavior

sam: ok will update the nsys perf artifact link once soak finishes: https://internal/builds/2228000000/nsys.zip :thumbsup:
